classification.difficultyReason: Apply successive percentages to different wholes, then include non-voters when finding the population complement.

content.prompt: In an election in a small island nation of $10\,000$ people, $80\%$ of the population voted. Of those who voted, $63\%$ voted for the New Liberation Party. How many people did not vote for the New Liberation Party?

answer.short:
$4960$ people.

Subtract the party's voters from the whole population, including people who did not vote.
answer.worked:
$$\begin{align*}\text{Number who voted}&=\frac{80}{100}\times10\,000\\\text{Number who voted}&=8000\\\text{Number voting for the party}&=\frac{63}{100}\times8000\\\text{Number voting for the party}&=5040\\\text{Number not voting for the party}&=10\,000-5040\\\text{Number not voting for the party}&=4960\end{align*}$$

This includes non-voters as well as people who voted for another party.
